ops.title: codex-ask launcher: replace the dirname exec with parameter expansion (22x under concurrency)
ops.description:
Measured on this host: /usr/bin/dirname costs 261ms serial and is serialized machine-wide at ~3.9 execs/sec, because Apple system binaries exec'd by path are inspected by the SentinelOne+Kandji EndpointSecurity extensions. A #!/bin/bash script is NOT serialized, and Go binaries under ~/.daemonkit cost ~6.5ms and are not serialized either. So the launcher pays nothing for being bash — it pays for the single dirname it forks, which is ~96% of its concurrent cost.

Current: ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
Fix:     case $0 in */*) d=${0%/*};; *) d=.;; esac; ROOT="$(cd "$d/.." && pwd)"

Verified on a working replica: 662 -> 288ms serial (2.3x), 7.48s -> 0.34s at 24-way (22x), rc=0. Pure parameter expansion, zero behavior change.

This was the amplifier behind a real fork storm on 2026-09-02: 56 concurrent codex-ask launcher wrappers plus 63 dirname children drove the machine to EAGAIN, which surfaced as PluginListError: [Errno 35] and every MCP server failing to connect.

ops.text: binrun-shim.sh:31 uses ${0%/*} parameter expansion, no dirname fork
install-binary-pinned.sh:26 and render-descriptor.sh:26 carry the same change
launcher re-rendered via cc-guides and the rendered output committed
